target_customer: Biotech and academic labs with computational biology teams that handle data from instruments, electronic lab notebooks and contract research organizations
problem: Dry-lab scientists lack life-science-specific data infrastructure, so they build their own schemas and pipelines and struggle with reproducibility.
business_model: B2B SaaS with a free plan for the scientific community and paid plans for biotech (pricing not found)
product_category: Life science data engineering platform (notebooks, database, pipelines)

founders.name: Emily Damato
founders.background_notes: YC page. Launch post: describes herself as a full-stack computational biologist who did wet and dry lab research at MIT.

founders.name: Madeline Schade
education: UC Santa Cruz, computer science and computer engineering
founders.background_notes: YC launch post: built a data capture system for a clinical trial of over 200,000 patients at GRAIL and worked on a system handling about 10 billion queries per day at Google.

competitors.name: Benchling
competitors.what: Research software for organizing wet-lab work; Mantle positioned itself as the dry-lab counterpart and integrated with it

competitors.name: Seqera (Nextflow Tower)
competitors.what: Platform for running and tracking Nextflow bioinformatics pipelines at scale
competitors.traction_then: five year anniversary news release in July 2023

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingestion from many lab systems, versioned datasets and reproducible pipelines is substantial data engineering, though the founders had built similar systems at GRAIL and Google.

defensibility.rationale: Storing a lab's data and pipelines can lock customers in, but open source pipeline tools and Benchling integrations lowered the barrier for rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A single weak profile claims Collate acquired MantleBio in August 2025. It was not corroborated and is not recorded as an exit.

market_need_then: The launch post says generic data tools missed life-science needs and that scientists were designing their own schemas. The founders saw the gap at GRAIL and Arsenal Bio.

branding.domain_note: Uses mantlebio.com, the name plus a bio suffix on a .com. Purchase history not found.

identity.logo: a plain M tile in directory listings, not confirmed as the official mark
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain scientific tone: bringing modern data engineering to the lab

branding.community_and_virality: Launched a free plan for the scientific community per a YC launch post title.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive bio suffix made the category clear and the free community plan is a goodwill move, but no brand press, community or merch was found, and Mantle Therapeutics and other Mantle names compete for search.

outcome_analysis: MantleBio's founders had direct experience of the problem from GRAIL and Arsenal Bio and the company grew to seven people in the Summer 2023 batch, with a seed round dated September 2023 by one database. The YC directory lists it inactive, and one unverified profile claims a 2025 acquisition by Collate, but no shutdown notice, acquisition announcement or post-mortem was found, so the outcome and its cause are not public.
notes: Funding rests on a single database (Caplight), which shows a seed dated 2023-09 and a total of $15M that no other source supports; the round amount is left null and the $15M is unverified. The Caplight listing also shows an unrelated headline about Caplight's own Series A. The Collate acquisition claim comes from a single AI generated profile on extruct.ai and is not recorded as an exit. Lexeo's deal for Mantle Therapeutics is a different company. Madeline Schade's education comes from her launch post. Website mantlebio.com returned HTTP 503. Exit type unknown.
